How screening works

From raw files to recovered revenue

Every audit batch moves through the same four stages, so no paid line goes unchecked and the evidence trail stays intact from import to recovery.

01

Ingest

Load claims, remittances, fee schedules, and contract documents. Every file is previewed and validated before the batch is saved — duplicates are blocked.

02

Validate

Data is normalized and each line is matched to the contract and rule version that actually applies — payer, plan, dates, and eligibility checked before any math runs.

03

Detect

Deterministic calculations compare expected vs. actual on every line, with explainable exception flags. Lines sort into matched, underpayment candidate, refund candidate, or needs review.

04

Resolve

Analysts verify the evidence, record decisions under their account, and track each finding from Flagged through Recovered or Closed — exported as reports your leadership can rely on.

Self-diagnosis

Where underpayments hide

Underpayments rarely look like denials — a partial payment arrives, the claim closes, and the shortfall goes unnoticed. These are the six places RCI actually screens for it, in plain language.

01

Contract rate & fee-schedule mismatches

The payer paid, but at a lower rate than your contract allows for that code, payer, and date of service. RCI compares every paid line to the contracted rate in effect on that date.

02

Units & modifier discrepancies

Units billed vs. units paid, or a modifier that changes the expected rate and was priced as if it weren't there. RCI checks units and modifiers against the rate that should have applied.

03

Adjustment-code (CARC) misapplication

An adjustment reason that doesn't fit the contract — for example a contractual adjustment larger than the contract supports. RCI recognizes all 407 CARC identifiers and preserves them in the evidence.

04

Patient-responsibility misreconciliation

Deductible, coinsurance, or copay amounts shifted to the patient — or double-counted — so the payer's share quietly shrinks. RCI reconciles patient responsibility before calling anything a variance.

05

Refund & recoupment exposure

Overpayments and recoupment requests sitting unreviewed until they become offsets. RCI surfaces refund candidates early, tracked separately, so your team reviews them before a payer acts.

06

Prompt-pay timing misses

Clean claims paid late under state prompt-pay rules, with no one tracking the clock. RCI screens timing against its 51-jurisdiction library so late payments are visible — analysts verify applicability before anything is pursued.

Traceability principle

Every production finding retains its source document ID, effective period, calculation inputs, rule version, evaluation timestamp, and reviewer disposition. Legal rules are never applied without a verified jurisdiction, plan, and product eligibility check.

Behind this view sits the national screening library: 51 jurisdiction profiles (50 states + DC) — 38 with preliminary baselines, 13 as reviewer workflows — and all 407 CARC identifiers recognized and preserved in evidence.

Contractual underpayment workbench

Line-level findings, calculated deterministically from your contracts — expected vs. actual on every line, with nothing priced by approximation.

Work the queue by finding type

  • All findings — the full screened batch
  • Potential underpayment — paid below the contracted expectation
  • Needs review — codes or terms the model can't price automatically
  • Matched — paid equals expected; no action needed

From finding to evidence

Select any finding in the workbench and its evidence card opens — the calculation, the rule version, and the source lines behind it. Batches export to CSV with financial columns in integer cents.

Claim-level evidence card

Every exception is explained with a reproducible calculation — so a reviewer, a payer, or an auditor can retrace exactly how the number was reached.

Service-line calculation

  • Units × contract rate = expected allowance
  • Expected − patient responsibility − paid = variance
  • Positive variance → potential underpayment; negative → refund candidate; zero → matched

Try the arithmetic yourself in The math section below.

Audit evidence

  • Rule reference and version applied
  • Source files the line came from
  • The calculation, shown step by step
  • Exception note and review status — human verification required

Validated before anything is labeled an underpayment

Allowed vs. paid, contractual adjustments, multiple remittances, patient responsibility, secondary payments, effective dates, modifiers, and payer/plan applicability are all checked before a line is called an underpayment.

An honest comparison

Why not spreadsheets?

Spreadsheets and variance-only tools each catch part of the picture. RCI's edge is different: every finding is traceable to a contract rate, a rule version, source evidence, and a human reviewer's decision.

CapabilityManual spreadsheet reviewVariance-only toolsRCI
Line-level contract comparisonSpot-checks — volume makes every-line review impracticalFlags totals that differ, often without the contract rate behind themYes — every line priced against the contracted rate in effect on its date of service
Evidence traceabilityDepends on who built the sheet; hard to retrace laterAlert without a reproducible calculation trailYes — calculation, rule version, source files, and reviewer disposition on every finding
Adjustment-code (CARC) checksCodes read by eye, claim by claimRarely — variance flagged without checking whether the adjustment code fitsYes — all 407 CARC identifiers recognized; code combinations gate the calculation
Prompt-pay screeningTracked manually, if at all, state by stateNo — timing is outside a paid-vs-expected modelYes — 51-jurisdiction screening library; analysts verify applicability and deadlines
Human review before actionYes, but findings compete with every other spreadsheet taskVaries — alerts often worked without structured verificationBuilt in — findings are candidates until an analyst verifies the evidence; nothing is submitted automatically
Recovery trackingA separate tracker someone has to maintain by handUsually ends at the flagYes — Flagged → Reviewed → Submitted → Resolved, tied to the same evidence ledger

A fair note: if your volume is small and your contracts are simple, a spreadsheet may be enough. RCI is built for when volume, payers, or contract terms outgrow manual review.

The math

A simple, inspectable formula

RCI's flat-rate model is deliberately transparent. Every candidate amount traces back to two lines of arithmetic and the contract rate you supplied — try it with your own numbers.

The flat-rate model

Expected allowance units × contract rate
Payer variance allowance − patient responsibility − paid

A positive variance is an underpayment candidate. A negative variance is an overpayment / refund candidate. Zero is a match. Flat unit rates are supported; complex reimbursement terms route to manual review instead of being approximated.

Adjustment codes gate the calculation: only CO/45 and PR/1, PR/2, PR/3 combinations can pass the code gate for this model. All 407 CARC identifiers are recognized and preserved in evidence — any other combination goes to an analyst with no automatic amount.

Trust & data protection

Built around safeguards — stated honestly

Your claims and contract data are sensitive. Here is how RCI is designed to handle them — described as the requirements the product is built around, not as certifications we claim.

How the workspace is scoped today

  • Practice-scoped workspaces — your data lives in your practice's account, not a shared pool
  • Authenticated staff roles — findings and decisions are recorded under the account that made them
  • Evidence retained per finding — source files, calculations, and dispositions stay attached to the claim line
  • Files previewed before saving — nothing enters an audit batch silently

Required before real patient data

Production use with real protected health information requires the full safeguard set on RCI's roadmap — these are prerequisites, not afterthoughts:

  • Tenant boundaries between practices
  • Encryption in transit and at rest, with access logging
  • Business associate agreements (BAAs) in place
  • Secure hosting and a completed security / threat review

What we do not claim: RCI does not present itself as HIPAA-certified or compliance-certified, and no such certification is implied anywhere on this page. If your compliance team needs the safeguard roadmap in writing before a pilot, ask — we'll share exactly where each item stands.

Two-minute check

Could revenue be leaking right now?

Answer six honest questions about how your practice checks paid claims today. Your result appears as you answer — nothing is stored or sent.

Revenue leakage self-check

Tap Yes or No for each question. There are no wrong answers — the point is to see where a second look would help.

1. Do you compare every paid claim line to the contracted rate — not just a sample?

2. Do zero-balance claims (paid, but possibly underpaid) get a second look?

3. Can you show the contract rate and clause behind every variance you find?

4. Are adjustment (CARC) codes checked against what your contract actually allows?

5. Do you track how quickly payers pay clean claims, state by state?

6. When a refund or recoupment request arrives, do you already know whether it's valid?

Answer the six questions to see your result

Each “No” marks a place where underpayments or refund exposure can sit unnoticed. Your score updates as you answer.

Honest limits

What RCI does not do

Trust starts with the boundaries. These limits are part of the product — not fine print — so your team always knows what a finding does and doesn't mean.

  • !
    Findings are candidates

    Every underpayment and refund finding requires analyst verification before it is acted on. Screening output is a starting point, not a determination.

  • !
    A refund candidate does not authorize a refund

    Refund candidates are tracked separately so a human can review, approve, and reconcile. Recovered / Refunded statuses are analyst assertions, not financial transactions.

  • !
    Preliminary baselines are not verified legal deadlines

    State baselines are screening references with source links and review dates. Operative authority and exact applicability must be confirmed independently — and no interest or statutory penalty amounts are computed.

  • !
    No live integrations, no automatic submissions

    There is no live EHR, clearinghouse, or payer connection, and no automatic appeal or refund submission. Files are imported; people decide what leaves the building.

  • !
    Coverage gaps are stated, not hidden

    13 jurisdictions run as reviewer workflows with no automatic baseline, and Washington is aggregate review only. Where the library has no baseline, a reviewer documents the authority and deadline by hand. No compliance certification is claimed.
